newsitem.title: USA: Crop Growers faces trial date on federal charges.
newsitem.headline: Crop Growers faces trial date on federal charges.

text.p: Crop Growers Corp said a tentative trial date for the single remaining federal charge stemming from a probe of campaign contributions to the brother of a former Clinton cabinet official has been set for the end of January.

A federal grand jury indicted the nation's second-largest crop insurer and two former executives in May for allegedly making and trying to hide illegal corporate campaign contributions to the brother of former U.S. Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy.
Earlier this week, Crop Growers said the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia dismissed 12 of the 13 counts against the company and 15 of the 18 counts filed against the two executives.
The company said it still faced a single count of conspiring to violate federal election laws, an allegation Crop Growers said it planned to fight.
Crop Growers said the independent counsel investigating the matter may decide to appeal the court's order.
The company's shares closed up 1/4 at 6-1/2 in Nasdaq trading on Tuesday.
